title: The Far Monsoon
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the flooded highlands of the Sareth Valley, disgraced mountain guide Kestrel Ishikawa is the only tracker desperate enough to take the contract. With river pilot Nadya Voss and her leaking boat, he follows a trail of abandoned gear into territory controlled by the Halvard Trust — an inheritance empire built on his own family's stolen maps. Kestrel discovers the survey team found proof that the Trust's land claims are forged, and that its heir, Edmund Halvard, will drown the valley rather than let it surface. The story ends with Kestrel surrendering his claim to the inheritance itself, choosing the ragtag crew around him over the power he could seize, as the monsoon breaks and the truth reaches the capital.
about_author: Lena Fairweather is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent a decade on river crews across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people the wilderness refuses to forgive.

chapters.title: Blacklisted
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Working a low-season port town, Kestrel is recognized and thrown out of a guide registry office — two countries now bar him. A government liaison finds him anyway: a survey team has gone silent in the Sareth Valley, leaving gear behind and no tracks. Pride wounded but wallet emptier, he takes the contract. Beat: bitter pride meeting reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He hires passage upriver from Nadya Voss, a sharp-tongued pilot whose boat takes on water faster than she admits. Their first night together is all friction — she knows his name and his blacklist. But when a squall hits, they work the bilge side by side without a word. Beat: grudging first respect.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the last survey camp: tents staked, food cached, instruments packed for travel — a team that left deliberately, not one that died. No tracks lead out. Kestrel reads the ground like text and finds one thing wrong: someone else arrived after them, wearing government-issue boots. Beat: unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Nadya's River
chapters.summary: Nadya's POV. Flashback woven through present navigation: how she lost her own license running cargo for men she shouldn't have, and why she knows the Sareth's drowned channels better than any map. She recognizes the route Kestrel is following and goes quiet. Beat: the cost of complicity, and the fear of repeating it.

chapters.title: The Trust
chapters.summary: Edmund Halvard's POV. In the valley's grand estate, the young heir of the Halvard Trust reviews flood-control schedules with cold precision. His steward reports a guide has entered the restricted zone. Edmund orders the sluice gates opened early — 'the monsoon is unpredictable.' Beat: elegant menace; power exercised without raised voice.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The river swells days ahead of forecast, stranding them above the gorge. Kestrel realizes the gates upstream are being managed — the flood is a tool. They shelter in a collapsed watchtower and find a survey team logbook hidden in the wall, half waterlogged. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Logbook
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Deciphering the damaged logbook by lamplight: the team traced boundary markers to their source and found the original survey plates — dated decades before the Trust claims to have commissioned them. The final entry: 'Halvard's man offered us money. We said no.' Beat: the stakes transform from rescue to exposure.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Trouble
chapters.summary: Nadya's POV. A storm forces them to moor at a fishing hamlet where Nadya once ran supplies. The villagers feed them, mend the boat's worst seam, and warn that Trust riders are asking about strangers. For one evening there is warmth — cards, stew, laughter. Beat: the found-family theme taking root before it's threatened.

chapters.title: Riders
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Trust riders reach the hamlet at dawn. Kestrel draws them off while Nadya slips the boat downstream; he escapes through terraced fields using old guide routes, barely ahead of gunfire. Reuniting soaked and furious, they argue about whether she should have waited. Beat: loyalty tested by survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Heir's Doubt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Alone in the archive, Edmund examines the original survey plates himself — and confirms they're genuine. His father built the Trust on forgery, and Edmund has spent his life defending a lie. He burns nothing, tells no one, and doubles down instead. Beat: corruption completing its work on a decent man.

chapters.title: The Drowned Channel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the logbook's coordinates, they enter a channel the Trust flooded years ago — beneath the water lie the ruins of villages that once held legal title. Kestrel recognizes the mapping style: it matches his grandfather's hand. The stolen maps were Ishikawa maps. Beat: personal history colliding with public crime.

chapters.title: What I Inherited
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with flashback. His grandfather was the surveyor whose plates proved the boundaries — discredited, blacklisted, ruined after refusing to sell. Kestrel's own blacklisting traces to the same machine. He confesses all of it to Nadya by firelight. Beat: shame transformed into inheritance of a different kind — the duty to finish the work.

chapters.title: The Middle Gorge
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Nadya's alternating POV. Running the gorge at flood stage to outride pursuit, the boat nearly founders; Nadya is swept toward a strainer and Kestrel goes in after her. They survive by the thinnest margin, boat holed, both shaken. Beat: trust sealed in near-death; the stranger becomes family.

chapters.title: The Survey Team Alive
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They find three members of the vanished team hiding in a limestone cave, kept alive by the fourth member — who turns out to be working for the Trust, feeding Edmund their location. A standoff in the dark ends with the traitor fleeing and the survivors joining the run downstream. Beat: allies gained, betrayal revealed.

chapters.title: Sluice Gates
chapters.summary: Survivor Mara's POV. An engineer among the rescued explains Edmund's plan: a controlled release timed to peak monsoon will scour the valley and destroy every remaining boundary marker — 'maintenance,' on paper. The only manual override is at the upper gatehouse, a day's climb away. Beat: a ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: The Climb
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel leads the ascent in driving rain along routes only he can read — this is what he was blacklisted for being best at. The team moves as one unit under his command, and for the first time in years he belongs somewhere. Beat: redemption through competence and care.

chapters.title: Gatehouse Standoff
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Edmund's alternating POV. At the gatehouse, Edmund waits with riders. He offers Kestrel everything: restoration of his license, his name cleared, a share of the Trust — if he walks away. Kestrel sees the trap and the temptation clearly. Beat: the corrupt bargain refused, but at visible cost.

chapters.title: The Release
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Edmund triggers the release manually; the override fails against flood volume. Kestrel's team diverts the surge through the old spillway Mara identifies, saving the lower valley but destroying the gatehouse. Nadya pulls survivors from the water as the world roars. Beat: climax — sacrifice, chaos, and courage at full flood.

chapters.title: What the Water Left
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Dawn after the flood: the diverted surge scoured the old channel, exposing the buried village foundations and boundary stones — evidence no longer deniable. Edmund, half-drowned and defeated, is taken into custody by the surviving surveyors' sworn testimony. Beat: exhaustion, grief for the dead, and the strange quiet after.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Refused
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the capital, lawyers confirm the Ishikawa plates make Kestrel heir to substantial claims in the valley. Officials offer him the Trust's reconstituted holdings. He signs the plates over to the displaced valley families instead, keeping only his grandfather's compass. Beat: theme resolved — power declined, inheritance honored differently.

chapters.title: Licenses Restored
chapters.summary: Nadya's POV. Both their names are cleared; registries offer positions in comfortable places. Nadya declines, and so does Kestrel. Instead they refit the patched, scarred boat — still leaking a little — and hire on the rescued surveyors as crew for a guiding outfit serving the valley people. Beat: found family formalized; home chosen over status.

chapters.title: The Far Monsoon
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing frame. A year later, guiding a client party through the green reborn valley, Kestrel pauses at the restored boundary stones. The monsoon arrives far off on the horizon, beautiful and unhurried. He checks his grandfather's compass, laughs at himself, and leads on. Beat: peace earned; the wilderness, finally, forgiving.
